rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (sensor spread x = -0.04..+0.04, kp 3.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.4) is the best raced design at 154.1. Line loss stayed near 1.0 per run on every track (0.95 to 1.00), and every run ended off_track except one oval finish. Iteration 2 raised kp to 3.5 without reducing line loss and dropped the score to 125.8, so kp is not the lever. Oscillation was 0.11 to 0.30, so the controller is not unstable. The line-loss mechanism looks geometric: the 25 mm tape can fall between 12 mm footprints on bends.

Change: this design is iteration 1 with one variable changed, geometry.sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016. Everything else matches iteration 1 exactly: sensor x = -0.04, -0.02, 0.0, 0.02, 0.04 at y = 0.03, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.4, line_loss last_direction. The earlier revise request was about a block that still showed kp 3.5 and sensor 0.012, so this block now matches the stated change. The footprint is the only difference from the best raced design, so any effect is attributable to it.

Expected result: line_loss_events falling toward 0.5 or below per run, and progress rising on the s-bend and slalom. Hypotheses: (a) a larger footprint keeps some tape under a sensor through the bends, so line loss drops; (b) if line loss stays near 1.0, the footprint is not the cause.

Next-step rules: if line loss is at or below about 0.5 and progress rises, keep 0.016 and test kd 0.3 to 0.4 (oscillation was 0.11 to 0.30). If line loss stays near 1.0, return to 0.012 and try a narrower spread (x = -0.03 to +0.03). If oscillation rises well above 0.3 on the oval, lower kd before changing anything else.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, so the footprint effect can be read separately from speed and damping.
